statusNote: Geopolitics and trade rules were researched on 8 Oct 2026, with sources in each row's About panel. The other numbers are still first estimates: facts already on this site plus judgement. Change any of them to match your own view.
plan: 100 is the AI data-center capacity that today's plans would add in 2027: what buyers have budgeted and suppliers have scheduled, with the shortages already known. Each supply number is the share of that plan one link delivers. Buyers want more than the plan (see Unmet demand), so a fall in orders only cuts what gets built once it is bigger than that cushion. Supply above plan is not counted: outcomes stop at 100.

drivers.label: Taiwan blockade

say.if: China blockades Taiwan

drivers.question: Will China blockade or quarantine Taiwan, stopping most commercial shipping for 30 days or more, starting before 31 Dec 2027?
drivers.resolves: Yes if major news agencies report that most commercial shipping to and from Taiwan was stopped for 30 days or more.
drivers.note: Forecasters see this as unlikely soon: Metaculus gives 2.5% to an attack or blockade during 2026 (861 forecasters) and Polymarket about 3% to a blockade by the end of 2026. This question is stricter (most shipping stopped for 30 days) but runs to the end of 2027, the PLA's reported readiness date. Signals are mixed: air incursions in September 2026 were well below 2024 and 2025 and Xi made a state visit to the US, while the China Coast Guard now patrols east of Taiwan without a break (ISW and AEI, 2 Oct 2026).
drivers.does: Applies The Chain's Taiwan blockade scenario from the day it starts: leading-edge wafers, CoWoS packaging and part of substrates, memory and rack assembly stop leaving the island.

src.t: Metaculus: Will China attack or blockade Taiwan during 2026? (2.5%)
Polymarket market on a blockade by the end of 2026, via Lines.com (about 3%)
ISW and AEI: China & Taiwan Update, 2 Oct 2026

markets.label: Blockade in 2026
markets.differs: Ends on 31 Dec 2026, a year before this question, and counts any sustained naval and air blockade, not only one that stops most shipping for 30 days.

markets.label: Military clash before 2027
markets.differs: Any military clash between China and Taiwan in 2026, which need not stop shipping.

markets.label: Invasion by 30 Jun 2027
markets.differs: An invasion rather than a blockade. Long-dated markets on rare events tend to read high, because betting against them ties money up until the end.

drivers.label: Gulf war drags on

say.if: the Gulf war drags on
say.of: that the Gulf war drags on

drivers.question: Will oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz still be below 75% of their pre-war level (about 20M barrels a day) on 30 Jun 2027?
drivers.resolves: The June 2027 monthly average from the EIA or IEA: yes if it is below 15M barrels a day.
drivers.note: Independent trackers put flows through the strait at 3.7M to 8M barrels a day in early October 2026, half of pre-war or less, even though Gulf crude exports as a whole were back at pre-war levels by late September through pipelines and ports that avoid the strait (Kpler). The June agreement expired on 18 Aug, ships have been attacked almost daily since 1 Oct, Iran says the strait stays closed until the US accepts its terms, and US officials expect airstrikes after the November midterms. A no needs a lasting settlement within about six months.
drivers.does: If yes, sovereign buyers order 20% less than the plan through 2027. If no, they order 15% more, as insurers and investors return to the Gulf.

src.t: Global Energy Flow: Is the Strait of Hormuz open? (7 Oct 2026)
Al Jazeera and Reuters: Middle East oil exports surpass pre-war levels (5 Oct 2026)

markets.label: Hormuz not back to normal by 31 Dec 2026
markets.differs: Counts ship transits (normal means a 7-day average of at least 60 a day on IMF PortWatch) rather than oil flows, and ends on 31 Dec 2026, six months before this question's date.

drivers.label: Helium shortage cuts chip output

say.if: a helium shortage cuts chip output
say.of: that a helium shortage cuts chip output

drivers.question: Will a leading chipmaker (TSMC, Samsung, SK hynix or Micron) say that a helium shortage has cut its output, before 30 Jun 2027?
drivers.resolves: Company statements, earnings calls or regulatory filings.
drivers.note: Qatar, about 30% of world helium, made no LNG and so no helium from 2 Mar 2026; a restart was set back by an explosion at Ras Laffan on 21 Jun, and LNG cargoes leaving the Gulf only recovered in September. Chipmakers have coped so far: Samsung and SK hynix signed extra US supply deals with Linde and Air Products in April, and we found no report of a leading chipmaker cutting output in seven months. The risk is a longer outage if the fighting spreads again.
drivers.does: From that day chip fabs lose about 3% of output (the helium part of The Chain's Gulf scenario).

The Elec: Samsung and SK hynix secure long-term US helium supply (8 Apr 2026)

drivers.label: Strike on a Gulf data center

say.if: a strike hits a Gulf data center
say.of: of a strike on a Gulf data center

drivers.question: Will a military strike damage or shut down an AI data-center campus in a Gulf state between now and 31 Dec 2027?
drivers.resolves: An operator statement or a major news agency report of damage or a shutdown caused by a strike.
drivers.note: Iranian drones hit AWS sites in the UAE and Bahrain on 2 and 3 Mar 2026, and two of the three UAE zones were still impaired in September. No data center has been struck since, but Iran named Stargate UAE as a target in April, and the UAE is splitting its 5GW campus into hardened sites across several emirates. Attacks at sea resumed in October, and US airstrikes expected after the November midterms could bring Iranian strikes on Gulf states again.
drivers.does: From that day sovereign buyers order 40% less, and less compute reaches the labs from Gulf sites.

src.t: Indoneo: Missile strikes force the UAE to scatter its 5GW AI campus (14 Sep 2026)
Global Energy Flow: Is the Strait of Hormuz open? (7 Oct 2026)

markets.label: US strike on Iran by 31 Dec 2026
markets.differs: Prices a new US strike on Iran this year (the ceasefire market's No side), the escalation most likely to bring Iranian strikes on Gulf sites. It says nothing directly about data centers.

drivers.label: China's mineral controls return

say.if: China's mineral controls return

drivers.question: Will China's export controls on gallium, germanium, antimony or rare earths be back in force for US buyers at any point before 31 Dec 2027?
drivers.resolves: MOFCOM announcements. China's pauses run with the US-China truce, which now ends on 10 Jan 2027 unless it is extended again.
drivers.note: The truce was extended on 24 Sep 2026, during Xi's state visit, by only two months to 10 Jan 2027, with no resolution on tariffs, technology limits or rare earths; we found no separate notice from China's commerce ministry yet, so the pauses are assumed to run with it. China's licences for dysprosium, terbium and yttrium, in force since April 2025, still slow supply. Severity stays at 0.3 of The Chain's worst case: during the 2024 and 2025 ban, supply kept moving through third countries at higher prices.
drivers.does: Applies The Chain's minerals scenario from the day controls return: gallium, rare earths, tungsten and indium go back behind licences. The hit lands hardest on lasers, through indium.

src.t: Phemex News: US-China trade truce extended two months to 10 Jan 2027 (26 Sep 2026)
Rare Earth Exchanges: truce extended to January 2027, rare earths unresolved (24 Sep 2026)

drivers.label: Tighter US chip export rules

say.if: the US tightens chip export rules
say.of: of tighter US chip export rules

drivers.question: Will the US impose new limits that cut AI chip sales to Gulf or other non-allied buyers (a new rule, or licences halted) before 31 Dec 2027?
drivers.resolves: A Commerce Department (BIS) rule, or company filings reporting halted licences.
drivers.note: The direction so far is the other way: in July 2026 Commerce moved the UAE into the same group as India, South Korea and Europe, so UAE companies and hyperscalers building there no longer need licences, citing its support in the Iran war; G42 and Saudi Arabia's Humain have had licences since November 2025. A new limit would most likely follow chips found going to China, or a change of course in Congress after the midterms.
drivers.does: From that day sovereign buyers order 35% less.

src.t: DCD: US eases AI chip export controls on the UAE (15 Jul 2026)
US Commerce Department: statement on UAE and Saudi chip exports (19 Nov 2025)

drivers.label: Chip tariff exemptions end

say.if: chip tariff exemptions end

drivers.question: Will the US end or narrow the Section 232 exemptions so that a tariff applies to most AI chips or servers imported for US data centers, before 30 Jun 2027?
drivers.resolves: A Federal Register notice or presidential proclamation.
drivers.note: A 25% tariff has applied to some AI accelerators since 15 Jan 2026, with exemptions for US data centers, startups and consumer devices. Commerce's Phase Two report was due on 1 Jul 2026 and is not public. Politico reported on 27 Aug that ending the exemptions and adding servers is under discussion, and on 2 Sep Lutnick said: "build in the United States, pay nothing; build nowhere, pay to enter the market". No rate or date is set, and duty-free allowances tied to US manufacturing could leave much of the trade exempt, which is why this is not higher.
drivers.does: From that day all buyers order 5% less capacity, because the same budget buys fewer servers.

src.t: Tech Times: chip tariff phase two confirmed by Lutnick (3 Sep 2026)
Tech Times on Politico's report: phase 2 targets servers and data-center carve-outs (28 Aug 2026)

drivers.label: Earthquake hits Japan's materials makers

say.if: an earthquake hits Japan's materials makers
say.of: of an earthquake hitting Japan's materials makers

drivers.question: Will an earthquake stop production for a month or more at a major Japanese maker of ABF film, T-glass, substrates, photoresist or wafers before 31 Dec 2027?
drivers.resolves: Company disclosures from Ajinomoto, Nittobo, Ibiden, Shinko, JSR, TOK, Shin-Etsu or SUMCO.
drivers.note: Japan's Earthquake Research Committee (26 Sep 2025) puts a Nankai Trough M8-9 quake within 30 years at 60% to 94.5% or more by one method and 20% to 50% by another, roughly 1% to 5% a year. Such a quake would reach makers in Gifu and Mie, a Tokyo-area quake those in Kanagawa, and Fukushima, home to glass-fibre and wafer plants, had M7+ quakes in 2021 and 2022. Only the 2011 Tohoku quake stopped these makers for months; later quakes stopped nearby plants for days or weeks. Severity stays at 0.5 because The Chain's scenario has several makers hit at once.
drivers.does: Applies The Chain's Japan earthquake scenario from that day: ABF film, T-glass, substrates, resist, wafers and test equipment.

src.t: Adnkronos: Japan revises the Nankai Trough megaquake probability (26 Sep 2025)

drivers.label: EUV supply stops

say.if: EUV supply stops

drivers.question: Will ASML's EUV shipments or servicing to leading chipmakers stop for 60 days or more before 31 Dec 2027?
drivers.resolves: ASML statements, or export-licence changes by the Dutch or US governments.
drivers.note: ASML has never stopped EUV shipments or servicing for 60 days. It expects to ship about 65 EUV systems in 2026 (44 in 2025) and 80 to 85 in 2027, and reports no supply problems; Dutch controls apply only to China. What is left are rare shocks: a fire or failure at a sole supplier such as Zeiss (optics) or Trumpf (lasers), a cyberattack, or war in Europe.
drivers.does: Applies The Chain's EUV scenario from that day: installed tools keep running but new capacity stops arriving.

src.t: Crypto Briefing: ASML can ship about 65 low-NA EUV systems in 2026 (15 Jul 2026)

drivers.label: Leading-edge wafers

say.if: leading-edge wafers hit their high case

drivers.question: What share of the leading-edge wafers (3nm and 2nm) that 2027 plans count on will foundries deliver?
drivers.watch: TSMC's wafers a month at 3nm and 2nm, against the demand its customers report.
drivers.note: The Chain rates this step tight, not short: 3nm is heading from 180k to 210k wafers a month, and 2nm from 90k to 110k by mid-2027. Plans are sized to scarcer links, so the central case leaves some slack.
drivers.does: Below 100, every AI accelerator is short by that share.

drivers.label: CoWoS packaging

say.if: CoWoS packaging hits its high case

drivers.question: What share of the CoWoS packaging that 2027 plans count on will be delivered?
drivers.watch: TSMC's CoWoS wafers a month and allocation comments from Nvidia, Broadcom and AMD.
drivers.note: The narrowest point of the chip chain per The Chain: about 130k wafers a month by end-2026 and about 260k by end-2028. Plans are sized to that ramp, so any slip cuts output directly.
drivers.does: Below 100, GPUs and custom accelerators are short by that share.

drivers.label: HBM memory

say.if: HBM memory hits its high case

drivers.question: What share of the HBM memory that 2027 plans count on will the three makers deliver?
drivers.watch: HBM bit shipments and allocation comments from SK hynix, Samsung and Micron.
drivers.note: Three suppliers, sold out, prices rising. The Chain rates it serious, one step below the scarcest links, so the central case leaves a little slack. The risk is HBM4 yields or qualification slipping.
drivers.does: Below 100, fewer accelerators can be packaged, by that share.

drivers.label: Package substrates

say.if: package substrates hit their high case

drivers.question: What share of the ABF package substrates that 2027 plans count on will be delivered?
drivers.watch: Capacity and lead-time comments from Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron and AT&S.
drivers.note: Short now, rated serious by The Chain. Ibiden is spending ¥500B through FY2028 for 2.5 times the capacity, so the central case leaves a little slack; new lines take two to three years.
drivers.does: Below 100, chip packaging is short by that share.

drivers.label: T-glass cloth

say.if: T-glass cloth hits its high case

drivers.question: What share of the low-expansion glass cloth (T-glass) that 2027 plans count on will be delivered?
drivers.watch: Nittobo's capacity additions and substrate makers' comments on glass cloth supply.
drivers.note: One maker, Nittobo, has about 90% of T-glass, and relief is not expected before mid-2027. A late ramp would leave the first half of 2027 short.
drivers.does: Below 100, substrates are short by that share and high-speed boards by most of it.

drivers.label: InP wafers for lasers

say.if: InP wafers hit their high case

drivers.question: What share of the indium phosphide (InP) wafers that 2027 plans count on will be delivered?
drivers.watch: Capacity announcements from AXT, Sumitomo Electric and JX, and laser allocation comments from Lumentum and Coherent.
drivers.note: The scarcest input in AI networking per The Chain. Six-inch capacity is meant to double by end-2027 and the shortage is expected to outlast 2027, so this has the widest downside of the chip links.
drivers.does: Below 100, lasers, optical links and cluster networks are short by that share.

drivers.label: Co-packaged optics in volume

say.if: co-packaged optics reach volume

drivers.question: Will co-packaged optics account for 10% or more of the new AI cluster switch ports shipped in 2027?
drivers.resolves: Shipment estimates from LightCounting or Dell'Oro, or Nvidia and Broadcom disclosures.
drivers.note: The Chain notes that the laser shortage is speeding up adoption.
drivers.does: Cuts any InP shortfall by a quarter, because each link needs fewer lasers.

drivers.label: Gas turbines

say.if: gas turbines hit their high case

drivers.question: What share of the gas turbines that 2027 plans count on will be delivered?
drivers.watch: Deliveries and backlog at GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy.
drivers.note: Makers can build about 60 to 70 GW a year against about 110 GW of orders, and slots are sold into 2030-31. Units for 2027 are already scheduled, so the risk is factory slips, not allocation.
drivers.does: Below 100, gas-fired power on the grid and on site is short. Other sources cover part of the gap.

drivers.label: Large transformers

say.if: large transformers hit their high case

drivers.question: What share of the large transformers that 2027 plans count on will be delivered?
drivers.watch: Lead-time surveys and deliveries at Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy and HD Hyundai Electric.
drivers.note: Lead times run up to four years and prices are up about 80%. The Chain calls this the slowest item to order for any new campus.
drivers.does: Below 100, grid connections are short by that share.

drivers.label: Grid connections

say.if: grid connections hit their high case

drivers.question: What share of the grid connections that 2027 plans count on will utilities deliver in time?
drivers.watch: Interconnection data from PJM, ERCOT and other grid operators, and campus energisation dates.
drivers.note: PJM's July 2026 capacity auction missed its supply target. Queues decide where campuses can go, and connection dates slip more often than they are beaten.
drivers.does: Below 100, the grid-fed part of new campuses (about two thirds of their power) is short by that share.

drivers.label: Three Mile Island restart delivers

say.if: the Three Mile Island restart delivers
say.of: that the Three Mile Island restart delivers

drivers.question: Will the Crane Clean Energy Center (the 835 MW Three Mile Island restart for Microsoft) be delivering power by 31 Dec 2027?
drivers.resolves: Constellation statements or the reactor's NRC operating status.
drivers.note: The restart is under way (The Money). It is small against the gigawatts needed in 2027 and matters more as a signal for 2028 to 2030.
drivers.does: Cuts any grid shortfall by 5% from the day it delivers.

drivers.label: Unmet demand

say.if: unmet demand hits its high case

drivers.question: How much more AI capacity would buyers take in 2027 than today's plans deliver, if suppliers could build it?
drivers.watch: Cloud backlogs at Microsoft, Oracle and CoreWeave, GPU rental prices, Nvidia lead times, and statements such as AWS saying capacity stays short of demand through 2027.
drivers.note: Every critical link in The Chain is sold out and AWS says capacity stays short of demand through 2027, which points to a real cushion. Its size is a judgement, and sceptics argue that part of it is double ordering.
drivers.does: Lifts what all buyers want above the plan. A fall in orders only cuts what gets built once it is bigger than this cushion.

drivers.label: Hyperscaler spending plans for 2027

say.if: hyperscaler spending plans hit their high case

drivers.question: What will Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle plan to spend on capital projects in 2027, as a percentage of their 2026 plans (about $840B together)?
drivers.resolves: Their 2027 guidance as it stands at mid-2027 (second-quarter results), midpoints added up.
drivers.note: 2026 plans: Amazon $220B, Alphabet $200B, Microsoft $190B, Meta $137.5B, Oracle $92.5B. Alphabet says 2027 will 'significantly increase' and AWS says capacity stays short of demand through 2027.
drivers.does: Hyperscalers place 70% of orders. Their orders move one for one with this number, measured against its starting central case.

drivers.label: Lab revenue growth

say.if: lab revenue hits its high case

drivers.question: Where will the combined annualised revenue of OpenAI and Anthropic stand at the end of 2027, taking today's level (about $135B) as 100?
drivers.resolves: Company statements and filings on annualised revenue at the end of 2027.
drivers.note: The two labs have signed about $1.14T of compute commitments against about $135B of revenue. In The Money, OpenAI needs about 34% growth a year just to break even on its commitments.
drivers.does: Weak revenue cuts what the labs can commit to. Neocloud orders move 0.3 for one with this number and hyperscaler orders 0.1 for one, measured against its starting central case.

drivers.label: Sovereign projects that go ahead

say.if: sovereign orders hit their high case

drivers.question: What share of the Gulf and other sovereign AI capacity announced for 2027 will actually be ordered?
drivers.resolves: Project announcements and operator statements at the end of 2027.
drivers.note: Gulf projects sit inside the war's strike zone and insurers have pulled back. This is the follow-through apart from the war, strikes and export rules, which have their own entries.
drivers.does: Sovereign buyers place 10% of orders. Their orders move one for one with this number, measured against its starting central case.

drivers.label: A pause in orders

say.if: orders pause

drivers.question: Will Nvidia report a quarter-on-quarter fall in data-center revenue for any fiscal quarter ending in calendar 2027?
drivers.note: Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 call pointed to about 70% growth in FY2028, which makes a pause unlikely but not impossible.
drivers.does: All buyers order 12% less from that quarter on.

drivers.label: OpenAI raises $30B or more

say.if: OpenAI raises $30B or more

drivers.question: Will OpenAI close new equity or debt funding of $30B or more between now and 30 Jun 2027?
drivers.note: OpenAI's compute commitments run far ahead of its revenue (The Money), so it depends on raising outside money.
drivers.does: If it does not, neoclouds order 15% less and hyperscalers 2% less through 2027, and less capital reaches the labs.

markets.label: OpenAI IPO by 31 Dec 2027
markets.differs: An IPO would count as funding here, but this market runs six months past this question's date and leaves out private rounds and debt.

drivers.label: Credit squeeze on AI builders

say.if: credit squeezes AI builders
say.of: of a credit squeeze on AI builders

drivers.question: Will S&P or Moody's cut Oracle to junk, or a large neocloud default on or restructure its debt, before 31 Dec 2027?
drivers.resolves: Rating agency actions and company filings.
drivers.note: S&P has Oracle at BBB-, one notch above junk, with $117B of bonds outstanding. CoreWeave carries $35B of debt with $6.2B of principal due in 2027.
drivers.does: From that day neoclouds order 45% less and hyperscalers 5% less (Oracle), and less capital reaches neoclouds, sovereign projects and labs.
